description: My name is Sanjay Subramanian and I am in 11th grade. I am interested in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, and their vast applications.
summary: Analog Atlas scores all 85,325 Earth land cells against 22 Moon and Mars sites using NASA LOLA, MOLA, Diviner and TES data, on four separate traits: terrain, sunlight, temperature and dryness. Click any place on Earth to see where it matches a site, where the match breaks, and which other Moon and Mars sites it resembles. The tool checks itself against classic analog sites: they rank at the 74th percentile on the traits they are cited for, versus 41 on traits they are not (permutation p = 0.0002). It also finds that no natural Earth site matches the lunar poles for temperature or sunlight, so it proposes a better-chosen set of sites that lifts Moon coverage from 0.33 to 0.63 for the same number of sites. Reports and share links are built in.
details:
Analog Atlas helps mission planners choose where on Earth to rehearse Moon and Mars operations. It compares every Earth land cell (85,325 at 0.5 degree resolution) with 22 Moon and Mars target sites on four traits scored separately from 0 to 1: terrain, sunlight, temperature and dryness. The overall score multiplies them, so one failed trait is never averaged away.

How it works: terrain uses NASA LOLA (Moon) and MOLA (Mars) elevation plus Terrarium tiles for Earth. Temperature uses LRO Diviner and MGS TES thermal inertia against WorldClim for Earth. Sunlight at the lunar south pole is computed from real LOLA terrain horizons and a year of Sun positions. Dryness uses WorldClim rainfall.

What you can do: pick a target, set mission priorities, rotate the globe, click any place to see a per-trait breakdown, find which Moon and Mars sites it resembles (reverse lookup), copy a share link, and download a site report.

Validation: classic analog sites rank at the 74th percentile on the traits they are known for versus 41 on traits they are not (p = 0.0002, n = 18 pairs). The tool also shows what no Earth site can supply: no natural site matches the lunar poles for temperature or sunlight, so it proposes an optimised set of sites (Moon coverage 0.33 to 0.63).

Limits: Earth air temperature stands in for surface temperature; illumination is modelled on a 1.9 km DEM; the validation sample is small.

Tools: Python/NumPy pipeline, Next.js and React, canvas globe, deployed on Vercel. AI was used in the process of completing this project.
